## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `e90f4f4b10740ec77b4d1f0b531ecc42a5693569`
Local-runs: none

Face: declaration (`Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`). No published schema and no governed path in the committed tree (3 files). Read: the full diff, card #29946 and its triage audit 6610340522, `referenceTargetOf` / `referenceCarrierOf` (`packages/spec/src/data/field-value.zod.ts`), and the dev report (`/mnt/project-files/issue-29946/os-dev-report.md`).

### ① Derived judgments

- **The fix reuses the one arbiter.** The private `RELATIONSHIP_TYPES` set and the raw `reference` read are gone. The related-list check asks `referenceTargetOf`, which answers for the reference value types (`lookup`, `master_detail`, `user`, `tree`), fixes `user` to `sys_user` by its type, and returns `undefined` for every other type. That is the judgement `$expand` and the referential delete walk read, so the route and the row query can no longer disagree. Correct.
- **The refusal is kept where it belongs.** A `user` field on a non-`sys_user` page, a `lookup` to another object, a `tree` on another object, and an unreadable carrier (the arbiter throws; caught here as "not a relationship") each still answer the located `400 invalid_relationship`. The message now names `user` and `tree`. Correct.
- **`tree` comes along** (flagged by the dev): a `tree` field references its own object, so a related list of children keyed by the parent field on the same object's page is a real relationship the row query follows. Accepted; it is part of the arbiter, not a second private list.
- **Regression origin:** 18.2.0 had no such route check (each related list was read through the list read); #27713 introduced it. Stated in the changeset.
- **Pins:** the card's reproduction through the real route (a related list on `sys_user` keyed by a `user` field answers with its rows), a `user` field on another page still 400, and lookup/master-detail unchanged. Ablations went red (2, then 1) and were restored, 32/32.

### ② Semver level

`'@objectstack/rest': patch`. No exported surface moves (`referenceOf` is module-private); the route accepts again what 18.2.0 served. Consistent with both declaration lines.

### ③ Boundary flags

- No `open_questions`. The second defect in the card body (a `url` action at `record_header`) is the `domain:ui` card triage split off; it is not touched here.
- The order's attribution block named `Fixes #29891` (the seat's template error); the dev wrote `Fixes #29946`. Correct.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-nzsli6`
Reviewed-by: `session_01WGufzibcN9oHa8kDbTTnL5`

**VERDICT: PASS**

### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/rest`, touching **6** documentable anchor(s).

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-6.mdx`  _(via /:object/:id/page (route, bridged from symbol referenceOf — its route source's handler names it))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-0.mdx`  _(via /:object/:id/page (route, bridged from symbol referenceOf — its route source's handler names it))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `master_detail (literal, 40 pages)`
- the SDK route bridge reached **61** of **219** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **158** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **158**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **103** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **19** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3b8c724cf21fe2b39b2c635c6ef2a2448fa952fb` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `de9d7c528bd48e3cec59b118c598c4e9b9ade67b` — the merge of head `3ca0ddde4314f0bbda3df23c6d92f14b70cb7891` into base `3b8c724cf21fe2b39b2c635c6ef2a2448fa952fb`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin de9d7c528bd48e3cec59b118c598c4e9b9ade67b && git checkout de9d7c528bd48e3cec59b118c598c4e9b9ade67b
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 3b8c724cf21fe2b39b2c635c6ef2a2448fa952fb 3ca0ddde4314f0bbda3df23c6d92f14b70cb7891 && git checkout -B drift-repro 3b8c724cf21fe2b39b2c635c6ef2a2448fa952fb && git merge --no-ff 3ca0ddde4314f0bbda3df23c6d92f14b70cb7891

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3b8c724cf21fe2b39b2c635c6ef2a2448fa952fb
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 3b8c724cf21fe2b39b2c635c6ef2a2448fa952fb` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.
